questions.stem: Calculate the relative formula mass (Mr) of calcium carbonate (CaCO₃). [Ar: Ca = 40, C = 12, O = 16]
questions.explanation: Mr of CaCO₃ = Ca + C + (3 x O) = 40 + 12 + (3 x 16) = 40 + 12 + 48 = 100. Remember to multiply the Ar of oxygen by 3 because the formula shows 3 oxygen atoms. A common mistake is to forget to multiply by the subscript number.

questions.stem: What is the relative formula mass of magnesium hydroxide, Mg(OH)₂? [Ar: Mg = 24, O = 16, H = 1]
questions.explanation: The brackets in Mg(OH)₂ mean there are 2 OH groups. Mr = Mg + 2 x (O + H) = 24 + 2 x (16 + 1) = 24 + 2 x 17 = 24 + 34 = 58. A common mistake is to only count one OH group and get 41, or to forget the hydrogen and get 56.

questions.stem: Calculate the percentage by mass of oxygen in water (H₂O). [Ar: H = 1, O = 16]
questions.explanation: Mr of H₂O = (2 x 1) + 16 = 18. Mass of oxygen in formula = 16. Percentage of oxygen = (16 / 18) x 100 = 88.9%. Water is mostly oxygen by mass, even though it contains twice as many hydrogen atoms, because oxygen atoms are 16 times heavier than hydrogen atoms.

questions.stem: A student needs to compare two iron compounds to find which has the higher percentage of iron. Which has the higher iron content: FeO or Fe₂O₃? [Ar: Fe = 56, O = 16]

options.text: They have the same percentage of iron

questions.explanation: FeO: Mr = 56 + 16 = 72. % Fe = (56/72) x 100 = 77.8%. Fe₂O₃: Mr = (2 x 56) + (3 x 16) = 112 + 48 = 160. % Fe = (112/160) x 100 = 70.0%. FeO has a higher percentage of iron. This is useful in industry when choosing iron ores for extraction.

questions.stem: What is the relative formula mass of sulfuric acid (H₂SO₄)? [Ar: H = 1, S = 32, O = 16]
questions.explanation: Mr of H₂SO₄ = (2 x H) + S + (4 x O) = (2 x 1) + 32 + (4 x 16) = 2 + 32 + 64 = 98. Make sure to count all atoms correctly: 2 hydrogen atoms, 1 sulfur atom, and 4 oxygen atoms. A common error is forgetting to multiply the hydrogen by 2, giving 97.
